question_text: Find the number of ways of selecting 3 vowels and 2 consonants from the letters of the word EQUATION.

recall_prompt: Say how you would count the selections of three vowels and two consonants from EQUATION — the two groups, the two selections and how they combine.
insider_note: EQUATION has five vowels — U counts even though it follows Q — leaving three consonants. The question says selecting only, so the answer stops at ⁵C₃ · ³C₂ = 30; an extra 5! for arranging answers a different question.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Separate the vowels and consonants
steps.margin_note: First mark. EQUATION: vowels E, U, A, I, O (5), consonants Q, T, N (3), all different. Select from each group: ⁵C₃ and ³C₂.
lines: EQUATION: vowels E, U, A, I, O (5),
consonants Q, T, N (3), all different.

recall.must_convey: That EQUATION has 5 vowels and 3 consonants, and the selections are 5 C 3 = 10 and 3 C 2 = 3.
accept: five vowels and three consonants, five C three is ten and three C two is three
separate the eight letters into five vowels and three consonants and select from each
ten ways for vowels and three ways for consonants
vowels five, consonants three, five C three ten, three C two three
count the vowels first, E U A I O

steps.why: The condition is on the two groups separately, so the letters must first be sorted into vowels and consonants; each group then has its own selection.
common_mistakes: Counting 4 vowels — EQUATION has five: E, U, A, I, O.
Treating U as a consonant because it follows Q.

steps.label: Multiply
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 10 × 3 = 30. (The question asks for selections, not words, so no arrangement factor.)

recall.must_convey: That the two selection counts multiply to give 30.
accept: five C three times three C two is thirty

steps.why: The vowel selection and the consonant selection are made together, so the counts multiply. No 5! appears because the question asks for selections, not words.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by 5! to arrange the chosen letters — that answers a different question (words).
